warning: TEST-ONLY: the answers are cases of v1.json, signed with its TEST-ONLY keys.

rules.rootsConfigured: Roots are configured when the roots option is given (any value but null), or when the SDK is a stable version (X.Y.Z, no -rc.N; Python compares its PEP 440 form, X.Y.ZrcN) and its build embeds at least one response-signing root. A release candidate that embeds the root is not strict for that alone: it bridges to signing through the latch.
rules.mode: The mode in force is required when roots are configured, whatever the option says; a when-present given explicitly (the option, or VAULTODY_RESPONSE_SIGNATURE when the option is not given) is then ignored, with one warning when the client is made. Otherwise: the option, else VAULTODY_RESPONSE_SIGNATURE, else the build default (DEFAULT_RESPONSE_SIGNATURE: when-present for a release candidate, required for a stable release). The client reports the mode in force (Node responseSignature, Python response_signature, PHP responseSignature()), also when it shows itself (inspect, repr, toJSON, __debugInfo).
rules.unsigned: An answer with none of the four x-api-response-* headers is refused as missing when the mode in force is required or the origin is latched. Otherwise it is accepted as absent, with unsigned_response_accepted and one warning the first time (once per client).
rules.signed: An answer with at least one of the four headers is always checked: valid is verified; a failure raises response_verification_failed and ResponseVerificationError with its reason, never retried; no root to check it with (no roots option and none embedded) is ConfigurationError, with no response_verification_failed.
rules.latch: Any answer with at least one of the four headers latches its origin, verified or not, before anything is thrown: { latchedAt: now, rootId: the root that verified it, or null when it did not verify }, stored with the pins (vault-keys-file-v1.json), then response_signature_latched with the latch as stored. Set once, never cleared: an origin latched before is not latched again, and raises no event.
rules.order: Events in this order: response_signature_latched, then response_verification_failed or unsigned_response_accepted.
rules.writes: Before the first write to an origin, a client whose roots are configured and whose origin is not latched yet makes one signed read (GET /api-keys/current/signing-keys, the key-pair check when a signer is set): against an origin that does not sign, the write fails before it is sent instead of running unverified (no vector; each language tests it against its mock gateway).

caseFormat.config: { name, rootsOption, embeddedRoots, version, buildDefault, option } → expected { mode, warning }. rootsOption: whether the roots option is given; embeddedRoots: whether the build embeds a root; version: the SDK version; buildDefault: DEFAULT_RESPONSE_SIGNATURE; option: the responseSignature option (null: not given, and no VAULTODY_RESPONSE_SIGNATURE). mode: the mode in force; warning: whether the one "when-present is ignored" warning is logged.
caseFormat.answers: { name, mode, roots, latchedBefore, answer } → expected { result, latch, events }. mode: the mode in force; roots: whether the client has the case's pinnedRoots to check a signature with (a client built from its configuration: required with roots is the roots option, when-present with roots a release candidate embedding them, required without roots responseSignature required); latchedBefore: the store holds the latch { latchedAt: 1794200000, rootId: the current root } for the origin; answer: "unsigned" (v1.json missing_all) or a v1.json case, whose verify.request, verify.response and verify.now are used. result: "verified", "absent", { error: reason } (ResponseVerificationError) or { configurationError: true }; latch: the store's latch for the origin after the answer, or null; events: the security event types raised, in order.

config.name: release_candidate_default
config.description: A release candidate with nothing configured: when-present, the bridge until production signs.

config.name: release_candidate_required
config.description: responseSignature required: strict from the start.

config.name: release_candidate_when_present_given
config.description: when-present given and no roots: kept.

config.name: roots_option
config.description: The roots option given: strict, so a signature stripped from the first answer on is refused.

config.name: roots_option_when_present_ignored
config.description: The roots option and when-present: strict all the same, and one warning that when-present is ignored.

config.name: roots_option_required
config.description: The roots option and required: strict, no warning.

config.name: release_candidate_embedded_root
config.description: A release candidate that embeds the root: when-present, so it bridges to signing; the first signed answer latches.

config.name: release_candidate_embedded_root_when_present
config.description: A release candidate that embeds the root, when-present given: kept, no warning.

config.name: stable_embedded_root
config.description: A stable release embeds the root: strict.

config.name: stable_embedded_root_when_present_ignored
config.description: A stable release with an embedded root and when-present given: strict, one warning.

config.name: stable_embedded_root_old_default
config.description: A stable version that embeds the root is strict even if its build default were still when-present (the release guard refuses that build).

config.name: stable_without_root_build_default
config.description: A stable version without an embedded root (the release guard refuses that build): the build default decides.

config.name: stable_without_root_when_present_given
config.description: A stable version without roots, when-present given: kept (nothing to be strict with).

config.name: release_candidate_two_digits
config.description: A release candidate numbered 12 is still a release candidate.

answers.name: unsigned_when_present
answers.description: An unsigned answer to a release candidate before the latch: accepted unverified, reported once.

answers.name: unsigned_when_present_with_roots
answers.description: The same with an embedded root (a release candidate bridging): accepted, no latch.

answers.name: unsigned_after_latch
answers.description: An unsigned answer from a latched origin: refused as missing; the latch is kept.

answers.name: unsigned_required_with_roots
answers.description: Roots configured and a signature stripped from the very first answer: refused as missing, nothing latched.

answers.name: unsigned_required_without_roots
answers.description: responseSignature required and no roots: an unsigned answer is refused all the same.

answers.name: signed_latches
answers.description: The first verified answer latches the origin with its root.

answers.name: signed_next_root_latches
answers.description: Verified with the next root: the latch names it.

answers.name: signed_required_latches
answers.description: Strict clients latch too: a store shared with a release candidate is strict for it from then on.

answers.name: signed_already_latched
answers.description: An origin latched before is not latched again: no event, the latch as it was.

answers.name: unknown_root_latches
answers.description: A signed answer from a root not pinned: refused, and the origin is latched with rootId null before the error.

answers.name: tampered_latches
answers.description: A signed answer that fails its check: refused, latched with rootId null.

answers.name: partly_stripped_latches
answers.description: Some of the four headers stripped: refused as missing, and latched (an attacker who strips part of the signature turns the client strict).

answers.name: partly_stripped_without_roots
answers.description: The same with no roots at all: the headers are checked before any root is needed.

answers.name: refused_already_latched
answers.description: A refused signed answer from a latched origin: no second latch.

answers.name: signed_without_roots_latches
answers.description: A signed answer to a client with no roots (a release candidate once production signs): ConfigurationError, and latched with rootId null, so a signature stripped from the next answer is refused.

answers.name: signed_without_roots_already_latched
answers.description: The same on a latched origin: no second latch.
